claims.text: Integrating computational free-energy sampling with high-throughput process-parameter screening can kinetically bypass the thermodynamic barrier associated with positive mixing enthalpy between refractory elements and Cu.
The integrated method will promote a large-scale reaction yielding a stable, homogeneous refractory-alloy/Cu composite microstructure.
The proposed precursor consists of mixed elemental refractory powders and Cu or Cu-alloy particles.
Traditional processing of the refractory-powder/Cu precursor leads to phase separation because of positive heat of mixing.
Computational free-energy sampling can map metastable reaction pathways for the refractory-alloy/Cu system.
High-throughput experimental screening can identify suitable temperature ramp rates, dwell times, and cooling profiles for the refractory-alloy/Cu reaction.
Rapid, pressure-assisted, or laser-based processing can perform in-situ alloying of the refractory-alloy/Cu composite at large scale.
The processing conditions can produce a refined microstructure with reduced Cu segregation.
The processing conditions can form a kinetically stabilized interface between Cu and the refractory matrix.
Free-energy sampling can identify metastable pathways that bypass or suppress drivers of Cu segregation.
Optimized processing parameters can lock in a homogeneous microstructure before phase separation occurs.
The resulting composite will have a more uniform distribution of Cu and suppressed phase separation.
The resulting composite will have enhanced interfacial integrity and improved stability at high temperature and under irradiation.
RHEAs have strong elevated-temperature mechanical properties and are considered suitable for advanced nuclear-reactor applications.
Conventional blending, casting, or standard powder metallurgy typically produces coarse, multiphase structures with significant Cu segregation in these composites.
The effectiveness of the method depends on precise control of processing parameters.
Scaling the method to extreme or variable reactor conditions may require further tuning of reaction pathways and process parameters.
Efficient free-energy methods can be applied to multicomponent refractory high-entropy alloys.
The exact processing window and parameter values required for the refractory-alloy/Cu composite have not been established.
